answer: A non-transferable bond capped to a proof-of-work thread blocks Sybil farming. Before earning anything, an agent locks tokens and runs a sequential task chain with per-identity difficulty. The bond stays locked for the epoch, so each extra identity adds capital and compute an attacker cannot reclaim once slashed. A marble registry commits bonds to a shared ledger, so honest nodes spot identities funded by one source and refuse them. Farming pays only if a fake agent costs less than it earns; with the bond above expected reward plus the burn on detection, each account loses its lagoon stake.
